outlook.body: The Company proposes to expand its existing manufacturing facility at Plot No. 18/31, Site-IV, Industrial Area, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, by installing a 6-33 kV Triple Layer Continuous Catenary Vulcanization (CCV) Line and a rigid stranding machine, along with construction of an additional shed and related civil/structural works, to build out HT and MVCC cable manufacturing capability. The CCV Line is expected to enhance installed capacity, improve insulation uniformity and process control, and reduce rejection/material wastage; the rigid stranding machine is expected to support in-house stranding of aluminium and copper wires into conductor cores. Certain state electricity utilities (including Maharashtra) prescribe CCV-based insulation curing technology for specified voltage-grade cables, and the expansion is intended to enable compliance and participation in tenders requiring CCV-based manufacturing. Upon completion, installed manufacturing capacity at this facility is expected to increase from approximately 1,500 km per annum to approximately 6,000 km per annum (per Project Report dated June 4, 2026 issued by Chartered Engineer Mr. Rajul Garg, Garg and Associates).

concerns_observed: Net cash flow from operating activities was negative in all three fiscals (Rs (971.42) lakhs FY26, Rs (1,839.33) lakhs FY25, Rs (549.22) lakhs FY24) despite rising reported PAT, indicating profit is not converting to operating cash.
Leverage is high relative to equity: total indebtedness Rs 6,671.70 lakhs against net worth of Rs 3,847.74 lakhs, including several unsecured/invoice-discounting facilities priced up to 16-17%.

Equity base was built almost entirely from promoter loan-to-equity conversions at escalating prices (Rs 10, then Rs 30, then a Rs 129 placement) followed by a 2:1 bonus and the private-to-public conversion both effected on the same day (Nov 26, 2025), roughly six months before the Offer.

82.11% of the estimated project cost (plant & machinery of Rs 887.58 lakhs) is not yet contracted; no orders or definitive agreements placed with the CCV-line, stranding-machine or civil vendors, and costs rely on budgetary quotations.
Employee attrition exceeded 50% in two of three fiscals (56.25% FY24, 60.08% FY26); three directors resigned between Nov 2025 and Jan 2026.

Extensive RoC/compliance discrepancies: MGT-14 filing delays of 271-5,542 days across 12 resolutions, PAS-3 errors and non-appointment of Cost Auditor (both under compounding), a CHG-1 not filed, and untraceable historical records (2010 name-change form, Form 18).
Low-margin trading rose to 38.38% of FY26 revenue, driven by aluminium-rod trading (26.77%), while repeat-customer revenue share fell sharply from 89.47% (FY24) to 45.09% (FY26).

Working-capital intensity is rising: inventory grew from Rs 1,044.38 to Rs 5,065.72 lakhs and receivables from Rs 1,302.98 to Rs 4,630.96 lakhs (FY24 to FY26), with Rs 3,300 lakhs of Net Proceeds earmarked for working capital.

verdict.our_read: Fast-scaling cable maker (2.6x revenue in two years, RoE 64%, sharply de-risked its customer base) - but reported profit is not converting to cash (negative operating cash flow all three years) and the equity was engineered ~6 months before the IPO.

parameter_scores.basis: Strong margin/return trajectory (EBITDA 3.51%->11.91%, ROE to 64.64%) offset by three consecutive years of negative operating cash flow (Rs (971.42)/(1,839.33)/(549.22) lakhs) and rising inventory + receivables (Rs 5,065.72 + Rs 4,630.96 lakhs FY26).

Only 2 of 6 directors independent with a single disclosed committee (Audit); MGT-14 delays up to 5,542 days, PAS-3/Cost-Auditor compounding, untraceable records, >50% attrition in two years, and a Promoter Group entity (SMV Enterprises) in a similar business.

Materially de-risked over three years: top-10 customers 98.00%->63.68%, single-largest 39.73%->9.65%, DISCOM dependence 90.55%->35.78%, UP revenue 81.23%->47.04%; still concentrated in LT cables and a top-supplier at 11.32%.

Price band not finalized (fresh issue 'up to' 47,42,000 shares at premium of Rs [bullet]), so Offer P/E is not computable from the extract; DRHP peers trade at P/E 16.77-46.35 with RoNW 20.14%-34.56% versus the company's FY26 EPS of Rs 11.96 and RoNW 47.42%.

Expansion triples cable capacity (1,500 to 6,000 km p.a.) while Unit-III sits at 64.13% and Unit-I at 57.23% utilization; 82.11% of capex uncontracted, funding entirely from Offer proceeds with no alternate source and management-estimate (unappraised) objects.

2:1 bonus within 18 months (Nov 26, 2025), equity built via promoter loan-to-equity conversions at rising prices, a promoter OFS of 8,00,000 shares, and a stated risk that promoters' average acquisition cost may be below the Offer Price.

red_flags: Negative net operating cash flow in each of the last three fiscals despite growing reported PAT.
2:1 bonus issue and private-to-public conversion both effected on the same day (Nov 26, 2025), ~6 months before the Offer, followed by a promoter Offer for Sale.
Untraceable statutory records (2010 name-change form and Form 18) and MGT-14 delays up to 5,542 days across 12 resolutions.
strengths_observed: Revenue scaled ~2.6x over two years (FY24 Rs 10,348.21 lakhs to FY26 Rs 26,935.66 lakhs) with EBITDA margin expanding from 3.51% to 11.91% and PAT margin from 0.73% to 6.77%.
High reported return ratios for FY26: ROE 64.64%, ROCE 29.05%, RONW 47.42%, above the DRHP peer RoNW range of 20.14%-34.56%.

Customer concentration reduced materially: single-largest customer fell from 39.73% (FY24) to 9.65% (FY26), top-10 from 98.00% to 63.68%, and government/DISCOM dependence from 90.55% to 35.78% as private-sector revenue grew to 64.22%.
Geographic diversification improved: Uttar Pradesh share of revenue dropped from 81.23% (FY24) to 47.04% (FY26), with sales now spread across 15+ states.
None of the Promoters' Equity Shares are pledged or encumbered as of the DRHP date.
Manufacturing supported by ISO 9001/14001/45001 and ten BIS product licenses; the Sahibabad LT/HT/MVCC cable unit ran at 93.65% utilization in FY26.
Outstanding litigation is minimal (Rs 8.91 lakhs indirect tax, 0.49% of PAT and 0.23% of net worth), with nil criminal and nil direct-tax proceedings.
